claims.text: A conformal nanoscale Ag coating on W particles will form a continuous Ag interlayer at W–Cu interfaces after consolidation.
A continuous Ag interlayer will reduce electron scattering at W–Cu interfaces.
A continuous Ag interlayer will reduce W–Cu interfacial thermal resistance.
Reduced electron scattering and interfacial thermal resistance will increase the composite's overall thermal conductivity.
The Ag-modified composite will retain mechanical durability comparable to the unmodified W–Cu composite.
The Ag-modified composite will retain irradiation resistance comparable to the unmodified W–Cu composite.
The proposed intervention is electroless deposition of an ultrathin Ag layer on W powder before spark plasma sintering.
Spark plasma sintering at around 900°C in vacuum or an inert atmosphere can preserve the intended nanoscale Ag interfacial structure when its parameters are optimized.
Minimizing interdiffusion is necessary to preserve the designed Ag interlayer.
Silver's high intrinsic thermal conductivity allows the Ag interlayer to act as an electronic bridge between W and Cu.
Keeping the Ag volume fraction low will ensure that mechanical durability remains comparable to the baseline.
Keeping the Ag volume fraction low will ensure that irradiation resistance remains comparable to the baseline.
The Ag-modified composite will have significantly higher thermal conductivity than an otherwise comparable W–Cu composite without interfacial Ag.
The anticipated benefits require the Ag coating to remain nanoscale and continuous.
Nonuniform plating, excessive interdiffusion, or unexpected reaction products could eliminate the anticipated enhancement.
